decisions.migration_notes: Generated module source paths and Graph-derived inputs now keep Microsoft Graph's original spelling. This change ships together with the verified-tree rename in the same release. Adopt both migrations together; no compatibility aliases are emitted. Every folder level takes the Graph route segment, for example identity-governance/entitlement-management/access-packages becomes identityGovernance/entitlementManagement/accessPackages and reports/daily-print-usage-by-user becomes reports/dailyPrintUsageByUser. Graph-derived arguments take the Graph property or URL-parameter spelling, for example black_and_white_page_count becomes blackAndWhitePageCount and user_id becomes user-id. Names that are not valid Terraform identifiers (such as @odata.type), reserved names and real collisions keep their existing argument name through an explicit Graph-to-input mapping, and generator controls and outputs keep their names. On Terraform 1.11 or later, update each caller's module source path and renamed arguments, keep module block labels and values unchanged, then run terraform init -upgrade and inspect a saved plan before applying. Resource addresses inside the modules are unchanged, so a source-path or argument rename needs no state move; the six replacement-trigger changes (groups, service-principals and subscriptions in v1.0 and beta) only follow the renamed inputs they reference. If you also rename a module block label, use a root moved block from module.old_label to module.new_label, or back up state and run terraform state mv with the exact instance addresses under exclusive backend access; do not do both. Download casing-migration.json and casing-migration.md from the release assets for generated and verified old and new paths, inputs and nested attributes; the JSON separates the mappings into generated and verified sections. This guidance does not establish provider or live Graph behavior for an upgrade.
decisions.summary: Preserve original Graph folder and input spelling in generated modules; publish with the verified-tree migration in the same release

decisions.migration_notes: Verified module folders and Graph-derived inputs now keep Microsoft Graph's spelling and case. The generated catalogs take Graph's folder and input casing in the same release. No compatibility aliases exist. 14 verified modules move: the folder levels identity-governance/entitlement-management, identity/conditional-access, role-management, directory/administrative-units and service-principals take their Graph route segments (identityGovernance/entitlementManagement, identity/conditionalAccess, roleManagement, directory/administrativeUnits, servicePrincipals), and each module that sat in one is removed under its old path and added under its new one (module_removed and module_added). Three hand mappings name folders that no Graph route segment names: catalogs/custom-extensions becomes catalogs/customWorkflowExtensions (the Graph collection catalogs/{accessPackageCatalog-id}/customWorkflowExtensions), the named-location modules become namedLocations/ipNamedLocation and namedLocations/countryNamedLocation (the Graph subtypes microsoft.graph.ipNamedLocation and microsoft.graph.countryNamedLocation), and role-management/directory/role-schedules becomes roleManagement/directory/roleSchedules (the module manages both roleAssignmentSchedules and roleEligibilitySchedules, which have no common Graph segment). Inputs that fill a top-level Graph property or a URL parameter take Graph's name in the modules whose path does not change (displayName, groupTypes, principalId, application-id, accessPackageCatalog-id; 40 removed and 24 required-added keys in these modules). The 14 moved modules rename their inputs by the same rule (for example ipNamedLocation display_name becomes displayName and is_trusted becomes isTrusted). In every module, an input that fills no top-level Graph property or URL parameter keeps its name. The renamed inputs reach conditions and replacement triggers through var references, so 12 precondition and postcondition findings and 7 replacement-trigger findings (plus the one for lifecycleWorkflows/workflows) are bound by digest: the conditions, messages and triggers are the same, only the input names in them changed. The snake_case attributes nested inside the object inputs of Graph-derived verified modules take the Graph property they fill: 90 attributes of 26 inputs in 11 modules are renamed (for example app_roles[*].display_name becomes displayName, tasks[*].is_enabled becomes isEnabled, users.include_users becomes includeUsers, questions[*].is_required becomes isRequired, logic_app.subscription_id becomes subscriptionId, callback.timeout becomes timeoutDuration) and 13 stay with a recorded reason because they fill no single Graph property name or are Terraform-only (content_base64, authentication_strength_id, persistent_browser_mode, scope_rule, approval_timeout_in_days, duration_days, member_id, range_type, extension_id, extension_type). In the six modules whose path does not move (applications, assignments, accessReviews/definitions, lifecycleWorkflows/customTaskExtensions, lifecycleWorkflows/workflows, termsOfUse/agreements) this shows as 9 variable_type_changed, 9 validation_changed and 2 replacement_changed keys (the assignments one is the update trigger, which keeps storing the previous release's schedule_update shape so the upgrade sends no second adminUpdate); the moved modules carry it inside module_removed and module_added. Request bodies are unchanged: the modules build the same Graph bodies from the new attribute names, so there is no plan change beyond the argument rename. Each affected object input also declares the old optional attribute names (typed optional(any)) and rejects any non-null value with a plan-time error that names the new attribute, so a caller who misses a rename cannot silently fall back to the default (for example a dropped is_approval_required_for_add or session-control flag would otherwise default off); the digests of the variable_type_changed and validation_changed keys include these guards. Update each caller's module source path and renamed arguments, keep module block labels and values unchanged, then run terraform init -upgrade and inspect a saved plan before applying. A module's resource addresses do not depend on its folder or input names, so a source or argument rename needs no state move and no moved block; if you also rename a module block label, use a root moved block from module.old_label to module.new_label, or back up state and run terraform state mv with the exact instance addresses under exclusive backend access, not both. The release asset .release/casing-migration.md (and .json) lists every old and new folder, every input rename and every nested attribute rename per module, and each module's variables.tf shows its new inputs.
decisions.summary: Preserve Graph casing in verified module paths and inputs; publish with the generated-tree migration in the same release
